slides.extracted_text:
Problem Statement
Teachers cannot continuously perceive every student's engagement across an entire session. Observations are largely manual, subjective, and scale poorly for large classes or longitudinal comparisons.
Limitations of manual observation
Momentary, biased, and difficult to compare across students, topics, or weeks.
False assumptions from simple signals
Looking down ≠ disengaged. Could be note-taking, problem-solving, or device-based work.
Our response
Context-aware multimodal analysis that fuses visual cues, feedback, and performance indicators.

Proposed System & Core Idea
End-to-end prototype that processes sparse sampled frames and optional feedback, fuses heterogeneous signals, and produces interpretable engagement estimates and short-term forecasts for teacher support.
Visual pipeline (sampled frames)
Student detection, seat mapping, orientation, and activity recognition (CNNs)
Heatmaps, peer-interaction markers, and temporal aggregations
Feedback & fusion
Student feedback → NLP → categories (difficulty, pace, clarity). Fusion layer combines signals with prior academic data to estimate engagement robustly.

Context-Aware Student Engagement Analysis
Why naive gaze detection fails: Looking down can indicate note-taking, problem solving, or device use — not necessarily disengagement.
Naive approach
Looking away from board → Disengaged ❌ (high false-positive risk)
Proposed approach
Combine visual behavior + activity detection + classroom context + feedback + performance → probabilistic engagement estimate
The system estimates engagement probabilistically; it does not claim direct access to internal attention.

Student Feedback & Academic Performance
Optional post-class feedback is analyzed with NLP to provide semantic context that complements visual signals.
NLP-Based Feedback Categories
Understanding
Difficulty
Pace
Clarity
Interest / Examples
Questions / Confusion
Engagement vs Academic Performance (Indicators)
Four example patterns used as investigative signals — not automated judgments:
High engagement + high marks → consistent learning pattern
Low engagement + low marks → consider targeted support
Low engagement + high marks → investigate out-of-class learning
High engagement + low marks → participation without mastery; review content
These patterns are indicators for teacher investigation, not conclusive labels.

Context-Aware Peer Interaction & Distraction Detection
Detects repeated orientation and proximity across sampled frames, measures duration/frequency, and contextualizes with activity type (lecture vs. instructed discussion).
01
Detection
Track per-student orientation and proximity across sampled frames.
02
Contextualize
Combine with teacher activity and class plan (lecture vs group work).
03
Flag & Recommend
Flag possible off-task interactions and recommend teacher review; do not auto-punish or auto-segregate.
Example student summary: Peer interactions: 6 • Estimated duration: 8 min • During lecture: 7 min • Engagement trend: declining → Recommend teacher review.

Forecasting, Early Warning & Adaptive Intervention
Short-term temporal models identify likely engagement declines and propose evidence-based, teacher-led interventions.
1
Early disengagement detection
Trend example: 72 → 68 → 63 → 57% → System flags "Potential engagement decline" and suggests interactive interventions.
2
Intervention suggestions
Ask a question, short quiz, 2-min discussion, targeted example, quick formative check.
3
Long-term analysis
Combine weekly engagement and marks to identify students who may need sustained support (e.g., Week1: 52%→Week4: 74% with marks trend).
The AI recommends actions; the teacher retains final authority and contextual judgment.
